entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ricardo Miró Denis (1883–1940) was a Panamanian poet widely regarded as the nation’s national poet, whose verses shaped patriotic feeling around independence, landscape, and civic identity. Writing across modernista and early twentieth-century idioms, he gave Panama a lyrical canon distinct from Colombian inheritance.

Poems of longing, isthmian geography, and nationhood circulated in schools and public ceremony, making Miró a staple of Panamanian cultural memory. Diplomatic and journalistic work linked letters to state-building after 1903.

He remains the central poetic voice of modern Panama.
